children: BEFORE THE BELL: EUROPEAN FUTURES RISE LED BY AI COMPLEX
European shares were set to open higher on Thursday after suffering their biggest two-day slide since March, with the AI complex driving premarket gains as investors cheered Anthropic's
upsized IPO, priced above its initial range ahead of its Nasdaq debut later in the day.
Nasdaq futures
rallied 2% after Wednesday's modest gains, while chip stocks and other AI-related plays in Europe, including ASML
, Infineon
and Siemens Energy
, featured among the top gainers premarket. Shares in Soitec
were called 10% higher after the French semiconductor materials supplier beat earnings expectations.
Futures on the euro zone's blue-chip EuroSTOXX50
index rose 0.7%, while contracts on Germany's DAX (GDAXI) and the UK's FTSE 100
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
added 0.3% and 0.1%, respectively. Shares in Commerzbank
gained 0.8% on Tradegate after UniCredit
and Germany reached agreement on key sticking points in the Italian lender's takeover.
Steadying crude oil prices and a bounce from seven-month lows in London copper futures may also offer some reprieve to commodity stocks following this week's battering.
In Asia, however, tech sentiment was clouded after Tencent's

quarterly revenue growth slowed more than expected, sending the stock to their lowest in over two years. The Chinese tech giant said new US chip curbs would likely slow development of its next AI model. Amsterdam-listed Prosus
, Tencent's largest shareholder, fell 2.6% on Tradegate.
